gaps.info: EMG/NCS results showing evidence of acute denervation (e.g., fibrillations, positive sharp waves) and chronic reinnervation (e.g., large motor units, reduced recruitment) in multiple regions (cervical paraspinals, proximal and distal right upper limb muscles)
gaps.discriminates: ALS vs. MMN (which shows conduction block but no denervation outside blocked sites) and vs. cervical myelopathy (which may show root-level denervation but spares paraspinals)

gaps.info: Presence of both upper motor neuron signs (e.g., hyperreflexia, spasticity, Babinski) and lower motor neuron signs (e.g., fasciculations, atrophy, hyporeflexia) in the same region (e.g., right arm)
gaps.discriminates: ALS (requires UMN + LMN signs in same region) vs. pure LMN disorders (e.g., SMA, spinal muscular atrophy; or MMN) and vs. isolated corticospinal tract lesions (e.g., tumor, which usually lacks LMN signs)

gaps.info: Cervical spine MRI demonstrating ventral horn signal abnormality, atrophy, or intrinsic cord lesion (e.g., syrinx, tumor) affecting C5–T1 segments
gaps.discriminates: ALS (no structural MRI abnormality) vs. compressive/intrinsic myelopathy mimicking LMN-predominant ALS
